description: We’re AirAware, a Palestinian team, and we’re good at programming and analyzing data.
summary:
MarsWalk is an expedition planner for walking on Mars. It helps future crews plan safe surface trips before they go, and lets anyone rehearse that trip virtually on real NASA terrain.

Choose any place on Mars on a 3D globe, set your stops, and MarsWalk plans the safest route on foot or by crew rover. It weighs slope, radiation, ground temperature, sunlight and radio coverage. Because Mars has no GPS, it also forecasts how the astronaut will be tracked along the way: the suit's own step-counting, the habitat's radio, and real passes of NASA relay orbiters (MRO, Mars Odyssey, MAVEN-era relays) that fix the position and re-plan the route.

Then you can experience it: walk or drive the route in true-scale 3D, first person, or in VR with a phone headset, with a spoken guide explaining each step.

How we built it: we started in QGIS, clipping and checking NASA/USGS elevation and imagery (CTX, HiRISE, MOLA). A Python pipeline turned them into slope, radiation, temperature and line-of-sight maps. NASA JPL Horizons gives the real orbiter and Sun positions, stored in PostgreSQL. A FastAPI planner finds the safest path, and the browser shows it with Leaflet and three.js.
details:
Project Details

What it does. Marswalk is a route planner and simulator for walking on Mars. There is no GPS on Mars, so an astronaut a few kilometres from the habitat needs a safe route and a way to stay found and in touch. Marswalk plans that route on real NASA terrain, predicts how well the crew can be tracked along it, and lets you rehearse it in true-scale 3D or phone VR.

How it works. Pick any place on a 3D globe of Mars. The server builds a 178 km site from NASA MOLA elevation in about a minute (Jezero crater uses MRO CTX 20 m and HiRISE 1 m data). Eight map layers describe the ground: elevation, slope, radiation, relay-satellite blind spots, habitat radio coverage, sunlight and shadow, ground temperature, and the planner’s cost. The map is cut into 20 m cells, each cell gets a cost (walking time × slope penalty + weighted hazards), and a least-cost path search finds the safest route. Navigation without GPS combines three sources: the suit’s own step counting, the habitat’s radio mast (range and bearing while it can see the crew), and position fixes from the real relay orbiters MRO, Mars Odyssey, TGO and Mars Express, using their orbits from NASA JPL Horizons. Messages to Earth cross the real light delay and wait at the orbiter for the next pass.

Features.

  • Global site picker.
  • Eight data layers.
  • Three route styles (Safest, Balanced, Fastest).
  • A navigation forecast.
  • Satellite pass alerts with Doppler.
  • A radio to the habitat and to Earth mission control.
  • A crew rover.
  • True-scale 3D, a first-person walk, and phone VR with gaze controls.
  • A two-page PDF mission report with a go / no-go check.
  • A guided tour.

Impact. It turns NASA data into a planning tool for future crewed EVAs. It shows where a crew would lose contact, how far their position could drift, and when a satellite will find them again, before anyone goes.

Tools.

  • Prototype in QGIS, then Python pipelines (rasterio, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-image).
  • FastAPI server and PostgreSQL.
  • Leaflet, three.js and the browser’s speech engine.
  • Hosted on Google Cloud Run.

Creativity. We are AirAwareNetwork, a Palestinian, community-led IoT air-quality network. At home we keep sensors connected and located across a region; here we asked the same question on Mars. Every number on the ground comes from real data, and anything that is a model or an assumption is labelled as one in the app.
